correctness.rationale: The complete normalized DCT-II is orthogonal; its complementary two-row two-column block has determinant-squared D and trace T, yielding all squared singular values. The determinant is nonzero for any distinct nodes. For every nonendpoint pair, the elementary bound lambda_- >= 4/(5N) min(sin^2 theta) (cos theta_j-cos theta_k)^2, plus sine spacing and a strict endpoint upper bound, proves unique extremal erased pairs for N>=5. The six N=4 cases are compared exactly. Taylor expansion of trace and determinant at the endpoint gives 9 pi^6/(25 N^7). A standalone NumPy checker passed 5346 finite assertions and is supplementary only.

value.rationale: The exact worst-case two-erasure threshold is a natural conditioning invariant for critically retained Chebyshev–Gauss polynomial sampling. Although every pair permits reconstruction, only adjacent endpoint gaps create the sharp N^7 squared-condition blow-up; the theorem characterizes all erasure spectra, global extremizers and the nontrivial exact asymptotic coefficient. It connects sampling design and redundancy against missing nodes beyond elementary DCT orthogonality.
